Seq2seq resolved to exactly its two consumed components: the cell (LSTM 1997 - both encoder and decoder are built from it) and the decoder formulation (Mikolov's RNNLM 2010 - the paper defines its decoder as an RNNLM conditioned on the input). The sharpest coeval artifact so far: Cho et al.'s RNN Encoder-Decoder (arXiv June 2014 vs seq2seq September 2014), the single most direct predecessor, dropped at the year bound together with 8 other 2014 artifacts (Devlin NNJM, GRU, Neural Turing Machines, Memory Networks, the WMT'14 dataset itself, dropout, conditional VAE, Chandar et al.) - at year granularity the template seq2seq scaled is unrepresentable as its predecessor. Recipe components behaved as designed: gradient clipping and teacher forcing passed directness (both literally in the paper's training procedure) but failed the Q1/Q2 gate on honest partials - components of a leap, not leaps. Generic substrate rejected as such: backpropagation, BPTT, SGD, CUDA. Two existing nodes (Bidirectional RNNs, Graves soft window) were scouted and matched but rejected for this parent - Sutskever's encoder is a unidirectional LSTM over reversed input, so no false convergence edges; both remain correctly attached at Bahdanau. NPLM rejected as mediated via the RNNLM, its consumed descendant.

BRNN resolved to its single consumed component: the Elman network (1990), the 'regular recurrent neural network' the paper explicitly extends in two directions. One-survivor expansion, like GPT-2's. Coeval artifact: LSTM (1997) dropped at the year bound - BRNN and LSTM are same-year siblings and their famous combination (BLSTM) waited until 2005, so at year granularity the cell BRNN would later marry is unrepresentable at this level. The forward-backward algorithm was graded directness=partial - the two-pass template is structurally identical to HMM smoothing and the authors worked in that tradition, but the paper presents the construction architecturally without citing it; partial fails the gate honestly rather than forcing a verdict. The Elman advance arrived twice in scouting (as 'Elman recurrent network' and as 'Finding structure in time', its own paper title); the second was filed as mediated via the first so the graph keeps exactly one Elman node. TDNN rejected as the overcome prior state (the paper defines itself against the preset future frame); substrate discipline maintained (BPTT/backprop/SGD/Fourier rejected as generic machinery).

survivors_detail.name: Pascal-Fermat correspondence on the problem of points (1654)
survivors_detail.status: NEW (depth 13 - the run's first depth-13 node)
survivors_detail.note: The session-56/58 assigned direct hearing, discharged as an admission. The channel is documented in the primary record: Huygens heard of the correspondence's problems in Paris in 1655 (from Carcavi's circle; he met Roberval and Mylon, not Pascal), was not told the methods or solutions, reconstructed them himself, and verified his Proposition XIV against Fermat through Mylon and Carcavi in 1656 (letter to Carcavi, 12 October 1656). The tract's problem-set IS the correspondence's: Props. III-IX are the points problem; the five closing problems are in part Fermat's and Pascal's; the last (Gambler's Ruin) stems from the correspondence resumed in 1656. Judged as an artifact (the letters), not a person-channel: what arrived was the founding content (the problems and the two solution routes' existence), per the Ferraro discrimination. Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5/Q6/Q10/Q11/Q12 pass; Q4/Q7/Q8 partial (no cost collapse in the letters themselves; no interface; reach beyond games performed by the tract); Q9 fail. Verification: four attacks run (channel attack - Huygens never read the letters, rebutted on the problem-set identity + the dated 1656 junction; multiples attack on Q3, scoped to descent of the problem-set; leap-inflation attack on the sample-space gloss, rebutted on Fermat's own device; reversed component attack on the two routes) - outcome provisional per standing practice.

Pascal's recursive expectation method (1654) - MEDIATED via the correspondence, same ground: the recursion is one of the two routes the letters contain; Huygens founds expectation on his own fair-exchange postulate, not on Pascal's text, which he never saw.

De Meree's gaming problems (1654) - MEDIATED via the correspondence: the channel runs questions -> Pascal -> correspondence -> tract; de Mere proposed no method, and the problems were the tradition's standing problems (in print since Pacioli 1494). Instance + motive at one remove (the Sears-at-Howard shape), the posing recorded in full.

CARDANO, Liber de Ludo Aleae - DATE-DROPPED at resolve (both filings, L1/L7), and the substantive record stands in the dropped list and here: filed at its graph-conventional year 1663 (the dating session 58 itself established - written in fragments c. 1525-1565, discovered among his papers posthumously, first printed in the 1663 Opera Omnia), the year bound drops it against the 1657 parent before any merits hearing, exactly as the print chronology foreclosed it at Bernoulli. The circulation record fetched this session makes the merits moot on the documents in any case: no source documents any circulation of the manuscript to Huygens, Pascal or Fermat (the one thin claim that Galileo 'seems to have read a copy' concerns an unpublished reader of an unpublished text). Anticipation/parallel, NOT a channel - the brief's anticipated outcome, reached by the calendar rather than by evaluation. parent_name: IBM solder-bump flip-chip joining with copper-ball standoff (1962)
provenance: Session 73, expansion 2 of 2 (the frontier's second node per status after session 72R; expansion 155 of this session took the head, Fisher-Rao). Scouted, resolved, judged and verified from scratch by session 73.
grounding: Totta & Sopher, 'SLT Device Metallurgy and its Monolithic Extension', IBM J. R&D 13(3):226-238 (May 1969) - FULL TEXT read (bitsavers mirror): the practice's canonical design record. Substrate: alumina ceramic, screened-and-fired thick-film resistors and electrode lands coated 90%Pb-10%Sn (mp 300C, above the 183C next-level eutectic) 'to facilitate the attachment of chip semiconductor devices by reflow soldering'; chips NOT in hermetic cans - the face 'hermetically sealed with a thin film of glass'; terminal system = Al-Si stripes under the glass, Cr-Cu-Au pads sealing the glass's terminal holes (Cr adhesion; first 500A of Cu phased with the last 500A of Cr so the Cu-Sn intermetallic cannot spall; 1000A Au cap), soft-soldered Cu sphere terminals (0.005 +/- 0.001 in., electroless Ni 1.25um + Au 0.25um) providing stand-off - 'specific departures from previous interconnection metallurgy'. Glass: lead borosilicate frit (Drakenfeld E1527), centrifugal colloidal deposition, fused 560-570C just below the Al-Si eutectic (577C) - 'the earliest successful means for glass passivating a planar junction semiconductor wafer at IBM'; Al sintering automatic during fusing; Al-penetration problem and its solid-solubility explanation. Solder preplacement - five methods investigated and REJECTED (molten immersion, solder-wave machine, silk screening, mask ball deposition, electroplating: thermal shock crazed the glass, bridging, non-uniformity, loading cost, insufficient volume); chosen = vacuum evaporation of Pb-Sn (~38um) through masks, uniformity 'far better than any other method explored'. Cu spheres: commercial spherical copper powder (powder-metallurgy filter material, <$1/lb) screened, blended 10:1 with alumina, re-melted ~100C above Cu's melting point in hydrogen (surface tension re-forms near-perfect spheres), micrometer-separated to 0.005 +/- 0.0001 in., Ni/Au plated; one million spheres weigh 10 g; acknowledgements credit R. Ross (sphere fabrication), Langdon & Pecoraro (terminal pad concept), Hymes (ball terminal standoff - via US 3,303,393), Kuiper, Barson & Sturm. Joining: ultrasonic dicing first (slow/expensive), replaced by the slurry saw (Seto & Wing 1966 - postdates); automatic test/sort 0.3 s/chip; automated placement on pretinned electrodes; rosin flux; reflow ~335C belt furnace (nitrogen); joints may see several later reflows. The record's own contrasts: 1-mil TC gold wire <10 g pull vs ~300 g for a three-terminal chip joint; 'the manufacturing advantage that all joints on all chips on a module are solder reflowed at one time'; controlled collapse described as 'a significant recent development' ELIMINATING the copper ball (the child's modification, consistent with session 67). T&S's 19-item reference list's pre-1962 ancestry items: [1] Langdon, Mutter, Pecoraro & Schuegraf, IEDM Washington DC, 27 Oct 1961; [2] Perri, Lehman, Pliskin & Riseman, ECS Detroit, 2 Oct 1961. Totta, 'Forty Years of Flip Chips with Solder Bumps' (abstract, read): 'During the summer of 1962, IBM reduced to practice the glass passivated flip chip transistor with solder bump connections... 3 bumps per chip with a 5 mil copper ball embedded in each... From the beginning there was a common Under Bump Metallization (Cr-Cu-Au) and high Pb chip solder (95-97% Pb/bal. Sn)'. Puttlitz & Totta (eds.), Area Array Interconnection Handbook (Kluwer 2001), ch. 1 structure: 1.3 SLT - the birth of flip-chip packaging; 1.4 Early Ball-Connection Development (1.4.1 Gold Ball Terminals; 1.4.2 Wettable Terminal Pads; 1.4.3 Ball Collapse); 1.5 C-4 Development; ch. 2.1.2 'General Motors' Early Flip Chip' (Delco - coeval parallel; NO firm pre-1962 document in hand: not filed, used as multiples evidence in verification). F. Rent's IBM-internal interconnection observations of the 1960s; published form Landman & Russo, IEEE Trans. Computers 1971 - Stroobandt SLIP 2001 tutorial).
